The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.97,75,000/- for the injuries sustained by Ramaprasad in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2.
That on 28.10.2020, at about 7.00 p.m., the deceased-petitioner was working as a clerk in Uma Maheshwari Community Hall and Spiritual Center for the period from 2.11.2019 till 28.10.2020.

Due to the tremendous impact, the deceased-petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

After being discharged, the deceased-petitioner was taken care by his family members.
The petitioners have spent Rs.20,00,000/- towards medicines, treatment and 4.

sentences.text: 5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-05-AB-1263.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Bhanashankari Traffic police as per Crime No.3/2021.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
6. It is relevant to note that, during the proceedings of the case, the petitioner reported to be dead on 12.2.2024.
Thereafter, through necessary application, his legal heirs were brought on record, by making necessary amendment through due process of law on 14.3.2024.
Thereafter, amended petition has also been filed.
7. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court, remained absent and placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has appeared but not filed his written statement.

8. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1(a) placed her affidavit evidence, in lieu of examination-in-chief and examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.
Since the respondent has not appeared before the court to contest the case of the petitioner, the matter was set down for arguments.
9. Heard the argument of learned counsel for the petitioners.
And perused the materials available on record.

10. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, this court has framed the following points;

3 POINTS 1) Whether the petitioners prove that deceased-petitioner Ramaprasad N.A. had sustained injuries and subsequently died due to the accident that occurred on 28.10.2020 at about 7.00 p.m. near Uma Maheshwari Community Hall and Spiritual Center, Opposite MTR Stores, K.R. Road, Bengaluru?
2.

3. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the only legal heirs and dependants of deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate from whom?
5.
What order or award?

11. My answer to the aforesaid points are as follows:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative.

Point No.2: In the Negative Point No.3: In the Affirmative Point No.4: Partly Affirmative Point No.5: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S POINT No.1 & POINT No.2:-
12
As these two issues are inter-linked with each other, in order to avoid the repetition of facts and discussions, they are taken together for common discussion.
13. The facts leading to this case is that, during the lifetime of the petitioner by name Ramaprasad N.A. on the history of RTA, filed this claim petition claiming compensation.

But unfortunately,
during the proceedings of the case, he succumbed to death.
Subsequently, his legal heirs were brought on record, through due process of law.
14. On the other hand, respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court remained absent, placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 though appeared through his counsel, but failed to file his written statement.
15. On going through the above point, onus probandi is on the legal heirs of the deceased to place satisfactory and convincing evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
16. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1(a) has examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P9
. Ex .

Ex.P2- true copy of FIS.

Ex . P6
-notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex.P7-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P8-copy of voluntary statement of complainant,
Ex.P9-true copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by petitioner No.1(a), the S.H.O. of Bhanashankari Traffic police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 of I.P.C. & Section 134(A & B) R/W Section 187 of IMV Act.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC R/W Section 134(A & B) R/W Section 187, 146 R/W Section 196, 3(1) R/W Section 192 of IMV Act.
18.
The material documents remained unquestioned and unchallenged by the respondents.

The silence on the part of the respondents in connection with the case of the petitioners make this court to draw adverse inference against them holding that, they deemed to have admitted all the allegations made against them.

The respondents neither have not made an effort to come forward to file written statement in answer to the case of the petitioners nor made an effort to adduce rebuttal evidence to shaken the case of the petitioners.

19. In the light of the above detailed discussions, and by virtue of the appreciation of all documents available on record, it is crystal clear that, on the history of the RTA, during the life time of the Ramaprasad had sustained grievous injuries.
20. Another material aspect to be discussed herein, that whether there is a nexus between the accidental injuries sustained by the injured and his subsequent death.
In this regard, it is to be noted that, after the death of Ramaprasad, his legal heirs were brought on record, through due process of law.

In the amended petition, the legal heirs have not made an effort to narrate in detail, to prove the nexus between the injuries and death, through proper amendment, in connection with the subsequent death of the Ramaprasad.

Since, it is the duty of the legal heirs, to prove the nexus between the accidental injuries and death, by placing satisfactory and acceptable evidence for consideration.
21.

On perusal of the wound certificate marked at Ex.P10 goes to show that, he had sustained the follows;
1) Head injury --- Left parietal epidural haemorrhage and left temporo parietal contusion.
22. The doctor is of the opinion that the said injury is grievous in nature.

The petitioner has also placed discharge summaries as petitioner Ex.P11 to Ex.P14, which reveals that deceased-petitioner was diagnosed as Covid-19-recovered, post left FTP decompressive Craniotomy with SDH Evacuation Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia, Hypertension and admitted from 1.1.2021 to 8.1.2021

,
Ex.P12 shows the deceased-petitioner was admitted from 22.12.2020 to 1.1.2021 for Covid 19 moderate disease, post left FTP decompressive Craniotomy with SDH Evacuation Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia, Hypertension, Ex.P13 shows he was admitted from 8.1.2021 to 11.1.2021 for Ramaprasad N.A vs Shobha.M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119754440/
5

Left FTP craniectomy, chronic myelogenous leukemia, Ex.P14 shows that the petitioner was admitted from 28.10.2020 to 29.10.2020 for left parietal EDH and left temporaparietal contusion,
hypertension and recently diagnosed blood cancer.
She has placed disability certificate at Ex.P15 and medical certificate at Ex.P17.
23. Added to this, petitioners have not not placed, further treatment documents to show that there is nexus between the accidental injuries and subsequent death.
On the other hand, no outpatient documents available on record, from the date of the discharge till his death.
24. In connection with this aspect, on going through the material document Ex.P20 death certificate of Ramprasad, reveals that, he had died on 12.2.2024.
The alleged accident had taken place on 20.10.2020.
The medical documents are required in order to know the whether the deceased Ramaprasad was died due to the accidental injuries or not.
25. Even the petitioners have not made an effort to examine the doctors whose names are fully mentioned in the respective discharge summaries.
In the claim cases, non-examination of the material witnesses is not always fatal under this beneficial legislation.
Even non-production of post mortem report also not fatal.

But, when the claimants are stressing the point about the nexus, and other side is disputing the same, their duty is more to place convincing documentary evidence for consideration and also to come to the proper conclusion in this regard.

26. At this stage it is relevant to rely the following decision;
i) M.F.A No. 1143/2008, between Sri. G.K Mariswamy Setty V/S. Sri. Ramaswamy and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, it was observed and discussed that, the post mortem report of the deceased would have ideal piece of evidence to establish whether the problem persists for such a long time and that would be direct cause attributable to his death.

In the absence of the same, self serving statement on oath,
the same cannot be accepted.
ii) In anther decision, reported in A.F.O.O No. 79 80, and 81 of 1995 between Vijayalaxmi Devi and Othrs V/S. Ram Naresh and Others.

entities.text: Vijayalaxmi Devi and Othrs V/S. Ram Naresh and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"It was discussed that, in the absence of the P.M report, it is difficult to come to the conclusion that the death was an account of the accident"
27.
In the instant case the deceased petitioner was suffering from blood cancer before the accident.
If the petitioners have placed P.M. report, it would have ideal piece of evidence to establish whether the petitioner had died due to the accidental injuries or from leukemia.
In the absence of the material document, it is clear that the petitioners have failed to prove the direct nexus between the injuries and his subsequent death.

28. In the light of my detailed discussion held above, I am of the view that, the petitioners herein have placed satisfactory evidence to show that, consequent upon the accident, Ramaprasad had sustained grievous injuries.
But, to prove the direct nexus between the said injuries and his subsequent death, no satisfactory evidence is available on record.
Accordingly, I am answering the point No.1 in the affirmative and point No.2 in the Negative.

6 ISSUE No.2 & 3 :
29.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that the petitioners are legal heirs of the deceased petitioners.
She has placed Aadhar cards of petitioner No.1 (a) and the deceased at Ex.P18 to Ex.P19.
The said documents remained unquestioned by the other side.

30. Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, in the light of the discussions held on point No.1, the death of Ramaprasad, is not due to the accidental injuries and there is no nexus between the accidental injuries and the death of Ramaprasad.
In such a situation, the legal heirs of the deceased-petitioner are entitled to get loss of income during treatment period and medical bills.
At this stage, it is necessary to rely the citation reported in 2010 KAR MAC 557 between Somavva & Others Vs. Vijaya Kumar & Others.

entities.text: Somavva & Others Vs. Vijaya Kumar & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 31. In the above case, the injured was died during the pendency of the petition and his legal heirs were brought on record and his lordship held that, the legal heirs are entitled for medical expenses and loss of income during the period of treatment.

So, by virtue of the above said decision, if injured died during the pendency of the claim petition, then her legal heirs are entitled for compensation towards medical expenses and loss of income during the treatment period.

32. In view of observations made in the aforesaid judgment, in connection with the facts and circumstances of the case on hand, it is pertinent to note that, the legal heirs of the petitioners have placed medical bills marked at Ex.P16 to the extent of Rs.19,17,273/-.

Along with this, on going through the discharge summaries the deceased petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient from 29.10.2020 to 10.11.2020, 10.11.2020 to 11.12.2020, 11.12.2020 to 22.12.2020, 22.12.2020 to 1.1.2021, 1.1.2021 to 8.1.2021 and 8.1.2021 to 11.1.2021.
During the said period, there was a loss of income to him, while taking treatment as an inpatient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the legal heirs of the deceased petitioner are entitled to get Rs.75,000/- towards loss of income during the treatment period.
33. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.
Compensation heads Compensation Amount Medical Expenses Rs.19,17,273-00 Loss of income during Rs. 75,000-00 treatment period Total Rs.19,92,273-00 34.

Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.19,92,273/-
(Rupees nineteen lakhs ninety two thousand two hundred and seventy three only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S.
Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

sentences.text: As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-05-AB- 1263, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

36. To disprove this stand of this petitioners and to show that as on the date of the accident insurance policy was in force, no satisfactory and convincing evidence is available on record, from the side of the respondents.
Absence of the respondents before this court clearly speaks that, they deemed to have admitted all the allegations made against them.
Hence, the respondents cannot escape from their liability to pay compensation amount jointly and severally.
37. On the other hand, on going through the prosecution papers, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of the accident, insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was not in force.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, in view of absence of insurance policy and by virtue of the principle of master held liable as on the date of the accident.
Accordingly, I am answering the point No.3 is answered in the affirmative and the point No.4 is answered partly in the Affirmative.

POINT No.5:
38.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act as against the respondent No.1 is partly allowed with cost.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act as against the respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.19,92,273/- (Rupees nineteen lakhs ninety two thousand two hundred and seventy three only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners together with interest, the petitioner No.1(a) to 1(c) are entitle for equal share.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, entire amount shall be released to the petitioners 1(a) to 1(c) through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
